name: DROWN
tagline: Old SSLv2 still knows how to read modern TLS.
blurb: Servers that never disabled SSLv2, or that shared a key with one that didn't, could have their TLS sessions decrypted. The attack uses a dead protocol to read a live one.
logo_credit: DROWN logo by Sarah Madden, CC0, from drownattack.com.

nvd.description: The SSLv2 protocol, as used in OpenSSL before 1.0.1s and 1.0.2 before 1.0.2g and other products, requires a server to send a ServerVerify message before establishing that a client possesses certain plaintext RSA data, which makes it easier for remote attackers to decrypt TLS ciphertext data by leveraging a Bleichenbacher RSA padding oracle, aka a "DROWN" attack.
